committee: CC Public Health and Community Safety
overview: The Medford City Council Committee on Public Health and Community Safety is a municipal committee responsible for reviewing and drafting legislation on public health regulations, community safety standards, and municipal surveillance oversight. Between June 2024 and July 2026, the committee held 17 recorded meetings to address city ordinances, departmental reports, and civil protections. Over this period, the committee developed and reported out ordinances regulating wildlife feeding, vegetative overgrowth, rodent control, and reproductive and gender-affirming healthcare protections. It has also maintained ongoing oversight over annual surveillance reports from the police and parking departments and local procedures regarding federal immigration enforcement. At its most recent meeting in July 2026, the committee approved an ordinance mandating law enforcement identification and restricting on-duty officer masking.

threads.name: Wildlife feeding regulation
threads.summary: In June 2024, the committee reviewed legal advice and Board of Health feedback on a proposed wildlife feeding ordinance, authorizing Vice President Collins to revise the draft offline to clarify enforcement terms and feral cat rules [M01#1]. By August 2024, an updated draft was presented that established exemptions for bird feeders and registered feral cat caregivers [M02#1]. Following advice from Health Director O'Connor to designate sanitarians as enforcement agents, the committee approved the amended text and reported it out to the full City Council [M02#1].

threads.name: Overgrowth and rodent control ordinances
threads.summary: In September 2024, the committee approved motions to draft an overgrowth ordinance and amend existing rodent control regulations to enhance public health enforcement [M03#1, M03#2]. Initial drafts were sent for legal and departmental review in October 2024 [M04#1, M04#2]. The committee revisited both measures in October 2025 to consider solicitor redlines on regulatory placement and coordinate enforcement language with DPW Commissioner McGivern, voting to retain them in committee for technical updates [M11#1, M11#2, M11#3, M11#4]. In December 2025, the committee approved and reported out both measures, forwarding an overgrowth ordinance that redirects fines to the general fund and a rodent control ordinance establishing composting rules and tiered fines [M13#1, M13#2].

threads.name: Reproductive and gender-affirming healthcare protections
threads.summary: In October 2024, the committee initiated review of draft ordinances to protect reproductive health and gender-affirming care by limiting municipal cooperation with out-of-state enforcement [M05#1]. The ordinance remained in committee in February 2025 pending a formal legal review by city solicitors [M07#1]. In April 2025, the committee approved amendments narrowing the definition of city agents, removing documentation requirements from the gender identity definition, and refining the purpose statement [M08#2, M08#3, M08#5]. The committee then approved the amended sanctuary ordinance and referred it to the full City Council for adoption [M08#1, M08#5].

threads.name: Surveillance oversight and CCOPS reporting
threads.summary: In December 2024, the committee approved technical amendments to the Community Control Over Public Surveillance (CCOPS) ordinance to strengthen data destruction rules and eliminate certain law enforcement exemptions, reporting the measure out [M06#1]. Police Chief Buckley presented the 2024 Annual Surveillance Report in May 2025, detailing body-worn camera volume and audit results regarding civilian notification compliance [M09#1, M09#2, M09#5]. In May 2026, the committee reviewed parking department license plate reader data with Parking Director Sarah McDermod and kept surveillance reporting in committee to coordinate with police officials [M15#1]. In June 2026, Chief Buckley delivered the 2025 CCOPS annual report covering body camera recordings and external investigative data, and the committee voted to approve the report while keeping the paper in committee [M16#1, M16#2].

threads.name: Immigration enforcement accountability and Welcoming City tracking
threads.summary: In May 2025, the committee questioned Chief Buckley regarding federal immigration operations utilizing police department grounds [M09#3]. The committee subsequently approved a motion in October 2025 requesting the City Solicitor look into filing Freedom of Information Act requests to track detained residents, keeping the matter in committee [M10#2]. In November 2025, the committee reviewed the Police Department's Welcoming City Ordinance report and debated methods for tracking ICE detainer requests without compromising privacy, ultimately keeping the report in committee [M12#1].

threads.name: Law enforcement identification and masking standards
threads.summary: In February 2026, the committee reviewed a resolution regarding law enforcement identification and Fourth Amendment rights, voting to keep the paper in committee to collect input from police, legal advocates, and community organizations [M14#1]. In July 2026, the committee discussed and approved an ordinance that restricts on-duty law enforcement officers from wearing masks or disguises outside of narrow tactical, medical, religious, or weather exemptions [M17#1]. The approved ordinance also mandates visible officer identification and sets procedures for verifying the identity of individuals asserting law enforcement authority [M17#1].
